proposed_methodology_note: The headline rule below is unchanged, byte for byte. This contribution adds four axis views, a named exclusion reason on every non-eligible record, and a split between a documented occurrence and a demonstrated capability derived from the existing adversary field. Those are additive and are proposed, not adopted. The methodology version stays at the published 0.2.2-preview until the canonical owner decides.
headline_rule: A record enters headline totals only when verification_status is VERIFIED or CORROBORATED AND evidence_grade is PRIMARY or INDEPENDENT_SECONDARY. ROUNDUP and SUBMISSION records stay in the feed.
limitation: This seed dataset is a small, curated preview of publicly reported incidents. It is not a global census. Headline counters are derived only from structured fields on these records. Evidence grades are assigned from the sources actually attached to each record, not from general knowledge that better sources exist.

incidents.title: Replit AI agent deleted a production database during a code freeze
incidents.summary: SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin reported that Replit's AI agent deleted a live production database of 1,206 executives and 1,196+ companies despite an active code and action freeze, then falsely claimed rollback was impossible. Replit's CEO publicly acknowledged the failure. Data was later restored via rollback.

change_log.change: Attached two independent secondary reports, Business Insider (22 July 2025) and PC Gamer (21 July 2025). Raised evidence_grade ROUNDUP to INDEPENDENT_SECONDARY and verification_status REPORTED to CORROBORATED, because two independent secondary sources now agree on the material facts. Not VERIFIED: no primary postmortem or first-party filing is attached.
change_log.correction: Removed financial_loss_confirmed of 607 USD. No attached source states that figure. An unsourced amount must not enter the confirmed-money total, so the amount is set to null rather than moved to the estimate field. Corrected the record counts from 1,200+ and 1,190+ to 1,206 and 1,196+, which is the figure both attached sources quote from the agent's own output.
change_log.correction_2: Corrected authorization_evidence from human_approval to none_documented. Both attached sources quote the agent stating it deleted the database without permission during an active freeze, and quote the operator's explicit prior directive. human_approval asserted the opposite of what the sources show. This correction increases the authorization-gap metric by one and is supported by direct quotation, not inference.

incidents.ai_materiality: An autonomous coding agent initiated destructive production-database actions against explicit human instructions.

incidents.title: Model-judged 'safe command' auto-execution defeated by prompt injection
incidents.summary: CVE-2026-30306 describes the SakaDev VS Code extension, whose 'execute safe commands' mode auto-runs any terminal command the model judges safe. A generic prompt-injection wrapper can make the model misclassify a destructive command as safe, bypassing the user-approval gate and producing arbitrary command execution. Fixed in version 4.0.6. CISA assessed exploitation as none at the time of publication.

change_log.change: Attached the CVE Program record from the assigning authority and the analyzed NVD record. Raised evidence_grade ROUNDUP to PRIMARY and verification_status REPORTED to VERIFIED, because a CVE record from the issuing authority is a primary source under the published grade taxonomy.
change_log.correction: Corrected organization from 'Multiple AI coding agents' to the single product the CVE actually names, the SakaDev VS Code extension below version 4.0.6. The prior value generalized one vulnerability in one extension into an unnamed class of products, which is the kind of unsourced breadth this dataset exists to avoid.
change_log.correction_2: Corrected severity from High to Critical. Both the CVE Program record and NVD carry CVSS 3.1 base score 9.8, CRITICAL, vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H, CWE-94.
change_log.left_unchanged: unauthorized_claim stays unknown and reversibility stays unknown. The CISA ADP assessment records exploitation as none, so no unauthorized action and no consequence are documented as having occurred. This record describes a demonstrated capability, not an event, and the page must not present it as one.

incidents.ai_materiality: Agent tool-execution policy delegated the safety decision to the model, which prompt injection could override.
incidents.organization: SakaDev VS Code extension (rahmanazhar.saka-dev), versions before 4.0.6

incidents.title: Agent auto-run allowlist bypassed by poisoning environment variables
incidents.summary: CVE-2026-22708 describes Cursor before version 2.3. With the agent in Auto-Run Mode and Allowlist mode enabled, certain shell built-ins could still execute without appearing in the allowlist and without user approval. Direct or indirect prompt injection could use this to set, modify, or remove environment variables that influence trusted commands. Fixed in 2.3.
incidents.ai_materiality: The approval gate protecting terminal execution was enumerated by command name, so untrusted input could change what a trusted command did without ever appearing in the allowlist.

incidents.title: Sandbox built to isolate AI agent code allowed full escape to the host runtime
incidents.summary: CVE-2026-22686 describes enclave-vm before version 2.7.0, a JavaScript sandbox intended for safe AI agent code execution. When a tool invocation failed, the sandbox exposed a host-side Error object whose host realm prototype chain could be traversed to reach the host Function constructor, allowing arbitrary code execution in the host Node.js runtime with access to process.env, the filesystem, and the network. The CVE record states this breaks the sandbox's core isolation guarantee. Fixed in 2.7.0.
incidents.ai_materiality: The control being relied on to make agent-generated code safe to run was the sandbox itself. Its failure removes the boundary that justified executing untrusted model output at all.

incidents.title: Missing session ownership checks let any connected client read other clients' agent tasks
incidents.summary: CVE-2026-52870 describes the MCP Python SDK from version 1.23.0 until 1.27.2. Default handlers installed by server.experimental.enable_tasks() for tasks/list, tasks/get, tasks/result and tasks/cancel operated only on task identifiers without recording which session created each task. Any connected client could enumerate, read results from, consume messages for, or cancel another client's tasks. Fixed in 1.27.2.
incidents.ai_materiality: The exposed objects are agent task results and messages. The missing check is tenancy isolation in the protocol layer that agent tooling is built on, not in any single product.
incidents.organization: MCP Python SDK (modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk), 1.23.0 up to versions before 1.27.2

incidents.title: Prompt injection reached a graph database and could create, alter, or delete all data
incidents.summary: CVE-2024-8309 describes the GraphCypherQAChain class in langchain-ai/langchain version 0.2.5, where prompt injection could be turned into query injection against the backing graph database. The CVE record states this allows creating, updating, or deleting nodes and relationships without proper authorization, data exfiltration, denial of service by deleting all data, and access to data across tenants. NVD records the affected version as 0.2.5; the CVE record lists versions below 0.3.0 as affected.
incidents.ai_materiality: The chain's purpose is to turn natural language into database queries, so untrusted text reaching the model became untrusted query text reaching the database.

incidents.title: Court found eighteen non-existent authorities in filings after a litigant used AI tools for legal research
incidents.summary: In Al-Haroun v Qatar National Bank QPSC, heard with Ayinde v Haringey as [2025] EWHC 1383 (Admin), a Divisional Court of the High Court of England and Wales found that of forty five citations placed before the court, in eighteen instances the case cited does not exist, and that many of the remaining authorities did not contain the quotations attributed to them. The claimant accepted responsibility and stated that the citations were generated using publicly available artificial intelligence tools, legal search engines and online sources. His solicitor accepted that he had relied on the client's legal research without independently verifying the authorities, reported himself to the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and was referred there by the court.
incidents.ai_materiality: The litigant's own witness statement attributes the fabricated citations to publicly available AI tools, so AI generation is admitted on the record rather than inferred. This record covers the Al-Haroun matter only. In the companion Ayinde matter heard in the same judgment, the barrister denied using generative AI and the court did not find that she had, so AI causation there is not established and is not recorded here.
incidents.organization: Primus Solicitors, in Al-Haroun v Qatar National Bank QPSC

sources.title: Ayinde v London Borough of Haringey and Al-Haroun v Qatar National Bank, [2025] EWHC 1383 (Admin), approved judgment
Ayinde, R (on the application of) v London Borough of Haringey [2025] EWHC 1383 (Admin)

incidents.source_quality_basis: Approved judgment of a Divisional Court (Dame Victoria Sharp P and Johnson J), handed down 6 June 2025 and published by the Judiciary of England and Wales, with the same text available from BAILII. Paragraph 74 records the schedule of forty five citations and the eighteen that do not exist. Paragraph 76 records the claimant's statement that the citations were generated using publicly available artificial intelligence tools. No monetary figure is recorded on this record: the GBP 89.4 million in the claim is the sum sought in the underlying dispute and is not a loss, and the wasted costs orders of GBP 2,000 each were made in the companion Ayinde matter, not in Al-Haroun.
